question: Can an exact in-memory Kimi-K3 semantic-state snapshot exceed 200 effective warm-prefill positions/s without changing cold execution?
arms: M8 cold full-prompt snapshot, mutate live state, restore twice
M64 safe committed-prefix snapshot plus exact suffix
M1024 cold full-prompt snapshot followed by two full-cache restores
secondary_metrics: snapshot save and restore wall time
snapshot slot and aggregate allocated bytes
physical expert bytes and traffic identity where existing counters expose them
correctness_gates: permanent CPU fixture preserves recurrent conv/SSM, right-sized MLA prefix, final logits, and rejects malformed layouts atomically
live cold and restored greedy output IDs are identical
valid restores report the backend-confirmed cached prefix with no hidden cold fallback
safe suffix restore preserves registered traffic/output identity
repeated restore of the same slot remains deterministic
performance_gate: GO only if the qualified M1024 full hit reaches at least 200 effective positions/s; smaller arms establish exactness and do not satisfy the target alone
abort_conditions: wrong physical GPU or multi-owner topology
swap growth, OOM, or invalid snapshot admission
snapshot restore silently falls back to cold prefill
cold control no longer reproduces the retained production path

interpretation.GO: Correct in-memory reuse reaches the target and may be integrated into the production ponytail.
interpretation.NO_GO: Correct reuse works but misses 200 effective positions/s; keep only if the product latency gain remains material and the implementation stays lean.
interpretation.INVALID: Any topology, correctness, fallback, resource, or fixture gate fails; no performance conclusion.

scope: In-memory prefix and Agent Turn Cache only. Disk snapshot serialization and cold/aggregate prefill claims are excluded.
